rules.statement: Rules 7 and 8 of the Schedule to the Appeals (Privy Council) Ordinance have no application to a case where the decree, without affording any substantial relief or remedy, declares a right or status.
rules.supporting_quote: "I am of opinion that these rules have no application to a case of this kind. What is the decree which has been appealed against ? It is a decree declaring that a certain document is a genuine last will. How is that decree to be executed ? The kinds of decrees which a Court of original jurisdiction can lawfully enter in this Island are enumerated in s. 217 of the Civil Procedure Code. A decree which declares a will to be genuine does not fall within any of the heads A to F in s. 217. Such a decree falls under head G of s. 217 which provides : ' Or it (the Court) may, without affording any substantive relief or remedy, declare a right or status '."
